stem: Write $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}$, $-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}<x<\dfrac\pi2$, in the simplest form.
model_answer:
$\cos x=\cos^2\dfrac x2-\sin^2\dfrac x2$ and $1-\sin x=\left(\cos\dfrac x2-\sin\dfrac x2\right)^2$ [1]
$\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}=\dfrac{\cos\frac x2+\sin\frac x2}{\cos\frac x2-\sin\frac x2}=\dfrac{1+\tan\frac x2}{1-\tan\frac x2}=\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac x2\right)$ [1½]
For the given $x$, $\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac x2\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)$, so the expression equals $\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac x2$ [½]

A curve rising from $\left(-1,-\dfrac\pi2\right)$ through the origin to $\left(1,\dfrac\pi2\right)$
A curve falling from $(-1,\pi)$ through $\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)$ to $(1,0)$
